CALM-2404.title: Paginate long license lists in the mobile app so they load
CALM-2404.why: Long license lists on the phone currently stall or never finish loading, so a hunter cannot see what they already bought. Paging the list is the difference between a usable app and a dead screen in the field. Michigan needs this before staff tell customers to 'just use the app.'

CALM-2903.title: Mobile tech debt, upgrades, and go-lives
CALM-2903.why: The mobile app has to stay current through OS upgrades and client go-lives or seasons stall on last year's build. This is keep-the-lights-on work, not a new hunter feature. Every client on the app depends on it shipping on time.

CALM-3213.title: Ohio survey mobile changes required right after go-live
CALM-3213.why: Ohio's post-launch survey flow on the phone does not match what they sold. If hunters cannot complete or replace the survey from mobile, field staff take the call and the go-live looks unfinished. This is a launch fix, not a new product.

CALM-3460.title: Show revocations on business-customer mobile profiles
CALM-3460.why: Business accounts can be revoked like people, but the phone profile does not show it. A clerk or owner who only uses the app can keep trying to buy. Showing the revocation on mobile stops that surprise at the counter.

CALM-3481.title: Work rolled from Q2 into Q3
CALM-3481.why: This is leftover mobile work that did not finish in Q2, not new scope. It is here so committed items do not vanish between quarters. PayIt owns the list; clients should not brief it as a feature.

CALM-3491.title: Mobile release maintenance
CALM-3491.why: Each mobile release needs testing, store submission, and fixes so hunters are not stuck on a broken build mid-season. This is release hygiene, not a new screen. All app clients feel it when it slips.

CALM-3502.title: Move mobile builds from Azure DevOps to GitHub and Fastlane
CALM-3502.why: Mobile builds still depend on a pipeline we are leaving. If we do not move to GitHub and Fastlane, every client release gets slower and riskier. Hunters never see this; product managers will if a season build cannot ship.

CALM-3516.title: Sort and paginate available vs submitted surveys on mobile
CALM-3516.why: Michigan officers and biologists cannot tell submitted surveys from ones still on the device when the list is one long scroll. Sort and page so field staff find the right survey without calling support. This is a field-time saver, not a new survey type.

CVEH-2566.title: Minnesota vehicles go-live remaining work
CVEH-2566.why: Minnesota vehicles still have remaining go-live work. Until it is done, DNR cannot run boat and vehicle transactions in CORE as sold. Treat this as launch completion, not a later enhancement.

CVEH-2578.title: Ohio customer and login vehicle bugs needed for go-live
CVEH-2578.why: Ohio vehicle customers hit login and account bugs that block go-live. A hunter who cannot sign in cannot register the boat they showed up to title. These are launch defects, not a new vehicle product.

CVEH-2707.title: Louisiana web new-registration depends on delayed payments being trustworthy
CVEH-2707.why: Louisiana's web new-registration path is only safe if delayed payments can be trusted. If money posts late or twice, the agency eats the exception. This unblocks their registration flow; it is not optional polish.

FNCL-2182.title: Voids must not rewrite prior-day financial reports
FNCL-2182.why: Voiding a sale today can rewrite yesterday's financial reports, which finance cannot explain to auditors. Voids must land as new activity and leave history alone. Every state that closes the day on CORE reports needs this.

FNCL-220.title: Staff can sweep an agent’s full ACH balance by hand
FNCL-220.why: Agents can be left with an ACH balance finance cannot pull without a workaround. Staff need to sweep the full balance by hand when the automated path is wrong or late. Arkansas, Minnesota, Mississippi, Missouri, and Ohio all hit this at month-end.

FNCL-2298.title: Search and report expired gift certificates
FNCL-2298.why: Ohio gift certificates expire and then disappear from search, so staff cannot prove what happened. They need to find and report expired certificates without a ticket to PayIt. This is customer-service time, not a new tender type.

FNCL-2300.title: Record full or partial payments that are not ACH
FNCL-2300.why: Not every payment is ACH, but CORE still treats some cash/check/partials as second-class. Finance needs a full or partial non-ACH payment recorded cleanly so the drawer and the report match. Same states as the ACH sweep work.

LICS-2579.title: Find a survey response by confirmation number without opening the customer
LICS-2579.why: Staff should find a survey by confirmation number without opening the whole customer. Today they hunt through the profile and burn the window. Arkansas, Mississippi, and Ohio need this at the counter and in the back office.

LICS-2733.title: Warn when a harvest check looks like a recent duplicate
LICS-2733.why: Ohio harvest checks get entered twice when a hunter or clerk retries. A warning on a likely duplicate stops a double harvest on the books. Wardens and biologists rely on one check meaning one animal.

LICS-3002.title: Show county assessor contact on land profiles
LICS-3002.why: Missouri land profiles omit the county assessor contact people actually call. Putting it on the land record saves a hunt through another system. Landowners and counter staff both use it.

LICS-3021.title: Retire and reorder landowner types without breaking land profiles
LICS-3021.why: Agencies retire landowner types, but old profiles still point at dead values and then will not save. Staff need to reorder and retire types without breaking existing land. Minnesota and Missouri cannot maintain land rules without this.

LICS-3039.title: Weight draw odds by points without always serving highest-points first
LICS-3039.why: Mississippi wants draw odds weighted by points without always handing the tag to the highest-point hunter. That is a fairness rule they already sold, not a new lottery. Applicants will notice if draws still behave the old way.

LICS-3529.title: Fix land-profile data that does not persist across mobile, POS, and surveys
LICS-3529.why: Land entered on the phone, at the counter, or on a survey does not always stick. Hunters then buy a landowner permit on land the system forgot. Minnesota, Mississippi, and Missouri cannot trust landowner sales until this persists everywhere.

LICS-3930.title: Refresh the product catalog without a full rebuild
LICS-3930.why: Refreshing the product catalog today is close to a rebuild, so price and rule fixes wait. A safer refresh lets merchandising change products without a project. PayIt-owned; clients feel it as faster catalog corrections.

LICS-3931.title: Load customers with long histories faster in POS, licensing, and mobile
LICS-3931.why: Customers with long purchase histories freeze POS, licensing, and mobile. Clerks wait, hunters wait, and the line grows. Faster load is a counter-time issue, not a new report.

RESRV-1466.title: Educator API so Kalkomey / IHEA course completions post to CORE
RESRV-1466.why: Hunter-ed completions from Kalkomey and IHEA still do not post into CORE on their own. Educators and agencies re-key or leave certifications missing, and then the student cannot buy. Several states share this dependency.

RESRV-1543.title: Ohio print-template fixes required for go-live
RESRV-1543.why: Ohio event and class print templates are wrong for go-live. If the paper in the hunter's hand is wrong, the launch looks unfinished even if the screen is right. This is print correctness, not a new event type.

RESRV-1546.title: Customer mobile check-in and check-out at unmanned Class B ranges
RESRV-1546.why: Ohio Class B ranges are often unmanned. Hunters need to check in and out on their phone so the range can run without a roster desk. Without this, those sites stay on paper or stay closed to CORE.

RESRV-1677.title: Return vehicle documents when a Minnesota sale is voided
RESRV-1677.why: When a Minnesota vehicle sale is voided, the documents still look sold. Title staff then chase paper that should have rolled back. Returning documents on void keeps the file and the money in sync.

RESRV-449.title: Informational event pages with no attendee or volunteer signup
RESRV-449.why: Missouri needs event pages that inform without taking signups. Today every event wants attendees or volunteers, so they fake a class or skip CORE. This is a communications page, not a registration product.

SYST-2366.title: Choose Radar, ESRI, or Google for address lookup
SYST-2366.why: Address lookup quality depends on the vendor, and one vendor does not win everywhere. Agencies need to choose Radar, ESRI, or Google without a code change. Ohio and platform-wide sales all use addresses to tax, ship, and prove residency.

SYST-2818.title: Revoke business customers the same way as individuals
SYST-2818.why: Business customers cannot be revoked with the same tools as a person. A shop that should be stopped can still sell. Ohio needs the same revocation path for both.

SYST-3228.title: Print a full customer profile with license sales
SYST-3228.why: Ohio staff print a customer and do not get license sales on the page. They then print three screens or skip the file. One full profile print is what a warden or clerk takes to the window.

SYST-3781.title: Separate citation add/edit access from revocations
SYST-3781.why: Citation entry and revocations share access, so the wrong person can revoke or cannot write a citation. Ohio needs those jobs split. Officers write citations; a smaller set should revoke.

SYST-3821.title: Log every Control Center view of a customer SSN
SYST-3821.why: Ohio requires a trail when someone in Control Center views an SSN. Without a log, they cannot answer an audit. This is privacy evidence, not a new customer screen.

SYST-3855.title: Ohio customer and login bugs needed for go-live
SYST-3855.why: Ohio customer and login defects still block go-live. If a resident cannot sign in or the profile is wrong, nothing else in Q3 matters for them. These are launch bugs.

SYST-4327.title: Highest-priority security bugs
SYST-4327.why: Highest-priority security defects sit here so they are not lost under feature work. Clients will not brief this as a product; they will feel it if we skip it. PayIt-owned on purpose.

SYST-4575.title: Certification setup that keeps collected fields consistent
SYST-4575.why: Certification setup lets fields drift, so one class asks for data another never stores. Agencies then cannot compare completions. Keeping collected fields consistent is how hunter ed stays auditable.

SYST-4614.title: Map of active selling agents by location
SYST-4614.why: Leadership wants a map of who is actively selling, not a spreadsheet of every agent ever. Minnesota and platform ops use this to see coverage holes. It is a sales-network picture, not a GIS project.

SYST-4630.title: Work rolled from Q2 into Q3
SYST-4630.why: Platform leftovers from Q2, not new promises. They stay on the roadmap so committed work is not dropped. PayIt tracks the list.

SYST-4714.title: Mississippi vehicle print-template changes
SYST-4714.why: Mississippi vehicle print templates do not match what they issue at the counter. Wrong paper means a customer leaves with a document they cannot use. This is template correction, not a new title type.

CALM-1866.title: Clearer mobile home screen: primary actions, menus, and first-time guidance (part 1)
CALM-1866.why: Hunters open the app and cannot tell what to tap first: buy, check game, or find rules. This first slice puts primary actions, menus, and first-time guidance in the right place. Research said utility beats a new look—so we are not restyling for its own sake.

CALM-2905.title: Mobile app upgrades and maintenance
CALM-2905.why: Mobile OS and library upgrades so the app does not die on a new phone. No new hunter-facing feature. PayIt-owned maintenance that every app client needs.

CALM-3382.title: Mobile release maintenance
CALM-3382.why: Routine mobile release work for Q4: submit, fix, ship. If this slips, hunters stay on a stale build through fall. Not a product announcement.

CALM-3424.title: Enter and edit citations in the field from the mobile app
CALM-3424.why: Ohio officers write citations in the truck, then re-enter them later. Entering and editing from the mobile app is the field workflow they bought. Paper-to-CORE delay is the problem this removes.

CVEH-1378.title: Mark a vehicle sold, including buyers with no account
CVEH-1378.why: A sold boat or vehicle has to leave the seller's record, including when the buyer has no account yet. Louisiana, Minnesota, and Mississippi cannot close the sale if CORE insists the buyer already exists. This is how a private sale actually works.

CVEH-1575.title: Transfer-on-death successors cannot transact until they take title
CVEH-1575.why: Minnesota transfer-on-death successors sometimes transact before they take title. That is a legal miss. They must be blocked until title is in their name.

CVEH-1924.title: Stop duplicate registration numbers and reuse unused numbers
CVEH-1924.why: Duplicate registration numbers and wasted unused numbers show up on the water and in audits. Stop the duplicates and reuse the unused pool. Every vehicle client inherits bad numbers if we do not.

CVEH-67.title: Require boat inspections before registration when the rules say so
CVEH-67.why: Some boats cannot be registered until inspection is on file. Louisiana and Mississippi already have the rule; CORE still lets the registration through. Block it when the rule says so.

FNCL-2361.title: Finish delayed-payment work not required for first go-live
FNCL-2361.why: Louisiana delayed-payment work that was not required to open the door. It still has to finish so later payments do not sit in a half-state. Finance will own the exceptions until it does.

FNCL-279.title: Automatically lock agents after failed bank returns
FNCL-279.why: Failed bank returns should lock the agent automatically so they cannot keep selling on bad paper. Minnesota, Missouri, and Ohio finance chase this by hand today. It is risk control, not a new fee.

LICS-2158.title: One- to three-day fishing permit on a single product
LICS-2158.why: Missouri needs a one- to three-day fishing permit as one product, not three SKUs clerks forget. Visitors buy the short trip they actually take. Merchandising and the counter both get simpler.

LICS-2732.title: License start-time defaults, per-agent limits, and policy messages
LICS-2732.why: Missouri license start times, per-agent caps, and policy messages are still easy to get wrong at the counter. Defaults and limits need to match how they sell. This prevents a clerk from issuing something the rule does not allow.

LICS-2740.title: Hunt-draw maps and replacement harvest-check IDs
LICS-2740.why: Missouri hunt-draw maps and replacement harvest-check IDs are how a hunter knows where to go and how to check in if the first ID is lost. Wrong map or no replacement ID is a season-stopping call. This is operations, not a new draw type.

LICS-3001.title: Separate landowner bonus points by hunt type and county
LICS-3001.why: Missouri landowner bonus points are mixed across hunt types and counties, so a point earned in one place spends in another. Split them the way the regulation is written. Landowners will treat this as fairness.

LICS-3019.title: Manage a customer’s land from their profile
LICS-3019.why: Staff should manage a customer's land from the customer profile instead of a side database. Missouri clerks lose land when they have to leave the person they are helping. One profile, one place.

LICS-3032.title: Collect only the land details the agency uses (part 1)
LICS-3032.why: Missouri collects land details CORE still shows as empty cards and unused fields. Turn off what they do not use, keep land type, and save acres the way they measure them. This is configuration, not a new land product.

LICS-3064.title: Residency, contiguous acres, and landowner attestations
LICS-3064.why: Missouri landowner permits depend on residency, contiguous acres, and attestations that CORE does not enforce cleanly. Get those wrong and a permit is issued on land that does not qualify. This is eligibility, not a form tweak.

LICS-3575.title: CWD and deer-management permit updates
LICS-3575.why: Missouri CWD and deer-management permits change with the disease map. Product and rule updates have to land before those seasons open. Biologists and the counter will both ask if the old permit is still for sale.

LICS-3576.title: Camping stay limits on rolling day-windows
LICS-3576.why: Missouri camping stays are limited on a rolling window of days, not a calendar month. CORE still lets people overstay. Rangers need the system to count the days the way the rule is written.

RESRV-1380.title: Attach an organization to an event or class
RESRV-1380.why: Missouri events are run by organizations, not only by a person. Attaching an organization to the class is how they assign ownership and reporting. Without it, every class looks like a one-off.

RESRV-1381.title: Tag which agency division owns an event
RESRV-1381.why: Missouri needs to tag which division owns an event so Education and Protection are not sharing a pile. Filters and reports only work if ownership is on the event. This is org structure, not a new calendar.

RESRV-1556.title: Turn class skills, attitude, and scoring on or off by state
RESRV-1556.why: Class skills, attitude, and scoring are not used the same way in every state. Agencies need those pieces on or off without a custom build. Arkansas, Missouri, Ohio, Oregon, and others share the same class engine.

RESRV-458.title: Stop signup when an event is full; keep waitlists accurate
RESRV-458.why: Events still take signups after they are full, and waitlists lie. Stop the extra seat and keep the waitlist honest. Shared across the states that sell seats in CORE.

SYST-3491.title: Printed license and receipt template fixes
SYST-3491.why: Missouri licenses and receipts print wrong, which is what the customer takes home. Template fixes are go-live for paper. Do not brief this as a new license type.

SYST-4500.title: Readable notification history with actual email content
SYST-4500.why: Notification history is a list of labels with no body, so staff cannot see what the customer was actually emailed. Show the content. Missouri and platform support both need this to answer 'I never got it.'

SYST-4669.title: Issue the ginseng authorization permit in CORE
SYST-4669.why: Missouri issues a ginseng authorization that still does not live in CORE. Until it does, that permit is a side process. Put it on the same customer as everything else they buy.

SYST-4803.title: Remind customers before products expire
SYST-4803.why: Customers find out a privilege expired when they are already in the field or at the counter. A reminder before expiry is fewer angry lines and fewer lost sales. Platform-wide.

SYST-882.title: Buy licenses for other people in one checkout
SYST-882.why: Buying licenses for a spouse or child still means extra checkouts. One cart for other people is how families actually buy. Minnesota, Mississippi, Missouri, and anyone using household sales will feel this.

CALM-2939.title: Switch address lookup vendors (Radar, Google, or others)
CALM-2939.why: Mobile address lookup has to follow the vendor the agency picked (Radar, Google, or other). A wrong or dead vendor means residency and shipping fail on the phone. PayIt-owned switch work that every app client inherits.

CALM-3134.title: Clearer mobile home screen and navigation (part 2)
CALM-3134.why: Second slice of the clearer mobile home: navigation that gets a hunter to buy, check, and find without hunting through menus. Same research as part 1—make the job obvious, do not restyle for its own sake.

CALM-3383.title: Mobile release maintenance
CALM-3383.why: Q1 mobile release maintenance so winter builds still ship. Not a feature. App clients stay current.

CALM-3384.title: Mobile app upgrades and maintenance
CALM-3384.why: Q1 mobile upgrades and OS maintenance. PayIt-owned. Required to keep the store listing alive.

CVEH-117.title: Staff can correct registration start and end dates
CVEH-117.why: Staff issue a registration with the wrong start or end date and cannot fix it without a ticket. Louisiana, Minnesota, and Mississippi need a staff correction path. Customers should not wait on PayIt for a date typo.

CVEH-1375.title: Different vehicle powers by seller type (office vs retail)
CVEH-1375.why: A DNR office and a retail seller should not have the same vehicle powers. Louisiana and Mississippi already run that split; CORE still treats them alike. Wrong power means a dealer does an office job or vice versa.

CVEH-1404.title: Reject invalid VIN format before save
CVEH-1404.why: Bad VIN format still saves, and then every later document is wrong. Reject it before save. This is data hygiene every title shop will thank you for.

CVEH-1412.title: Fill make and year from the hull ID
CVEH-1412.why: Hull ID already knows make and year; clerks retype it and mismatch. Autofill from the hull ID for Louisiana, Minnesota, and Mississippi. Faster counter, fewer typos on the title.

CVEH-1420.title: One primary owner on each vehicle
CVEH-1420.why: Vehicles end up with two 'primary' owners and then every mailing and liability question is ambiguous. One primary owner. Minnesota, Mississippi, and platform vehicle clients.

CVEH-1571.title: Search and autofill lienholder banks
CVEH-1571.why: Lienholder banks are retyped every time, so names never match. Search and autofill the bank. Title staff stop inventing a new spelling of the same lender.

CVEH-1617.title: Standard reasons when more information is needed
CVEH-1617.why: When more information is needed, the reason is free text and unreportable. Standard reasons for Louisiana, Minnesota, and Mississippi so queues and letters mean the same thing. Customers get a clear ask instead of a vague hold.

CVEH-1685.title: Title mailing-address list for a date range
CVEH-1685.why: Mississippi needs a mailing list of titles for a date range to run the print vendor. Without it, they export by hand. This is operations for title-by-mail.

FNCL-1547.title: Accounting reports — next set
FNCL-1547.why: Minnesota and Missouri still need the next set of accounting reports they close the books on. If a report is missing, they keep a shadow spreadsheet. This is finance's month-end, not a dashboard for fun.

FNCL-1626.title: Accounting reports — additional states
FNCL-1626.why: Additional states need those same accounting reports, not a one-off for the first two. Louisiana, Minnesota, Mississippi, and Missouri all have to file. Same reports, more books.

FNCL-1635.title: Vendor statements: newest first, printable, skip vendors with no sales
FNCL-1635.why: Missouri vendor statements dump oldest-first and include vendors with no sales. Print newest first and skip the zeros so accounting can mail a statement. Small, and they will notice every month.

FNCL-2.title: Calculate sales tax on merchandise and fees (licenses can stay untaxed)
FNCL-2.why: Merchandise and fees need sales tax; many licenses stay untaxed. Today the cart cannot do that split, so agencies either skip tax or tax the wrong thing. Minnesota, Mississippi, and Ohio all have this mix in one sale.

FNCL-322.title: Report collected tax by Ohio taxing district (and home state if out of Ohio)
FNCL-322.why: Ohio has to report tax by taxing district, and by the customer's home state when they are not Ohio. Without that breakdown, finance cannot file what DOW owes the state. This attributes tax already collected; it does not invent a new tax.

FNCL-68.title: Clearer history of voids, refunds, and invalidations
FNCL-68.why: Voids, refunds, and invalidations are hard to follow after the fact, so clerks and finance argue about what happened. A clearer history is how you answer a customer and an auditor. Minnesota, Mississippi, and Missouri.

LICS-2157.title: Multiple attachments on a land record
LICS-2157.why: Missouri land records need more than one attachment (deed, map, letter). One file means the rest lives in email. Multiple attachments keep the land file in CORE.

LICS-2736.title: Clearer residency rules and display
LICS-2736.why: Residency rules are easy to misread on screen, so a nonresident buys a resident price or vice versa. Minnesota and Missouri need the rule and the display to match. This is money and eligibility, not copy-editing.

LICS-3018.title: Better land search results for staff
LICS-3018.why: Missouri staff search land and get results they cannot use. Better results mean they find the tract before the hunter leaves the counter. Search quality is a landowner-sale problem.

LICS-3020.title: Customer-facing property card on the web
LICS-3020.why: Missouri landowners should see their property card on the web the way staff see it. Today they call in because they cannot verify acres or type. Self-serve here cuts counter volume.

LICS-3031.title: Hide land editing from the sales counter
LICS-3031.why: The sales counter should not edit land; that is how acres get changed during a rush. Missouri wants land edits in the back office. Clerks sell; specialists maintain land.

LICS-3053.title: Keep land history when customer records are merged
LICS-3053.why: Merging two customer records today can drop land history. Missouri still needs to know which land that person used. History has to survive the merge.

LICS-3054.title: Show land used on a past sale
LICS-3054.why: Staff cannot see which land was used on a past sale, so they re-ask the hunter every year. Show it. Missouri landowner renewals get faster and more accurate.

LICS-3055.title: Land updates appear the same on web, counter, and back office
LICS-3055.why: A land change on the web does not always show at the counter or in the back office. Missouri will sell on stale acres if those three stay out of sync. Same land, same picture everywhere.

LICS-3062.title: Simpler land fields for landowners (part 2)
LICS-3062.why: Second slice of simpler land fields for Missouri landowners: collect what the rule needs, hide the rest. Landowners abandon the form when it looks like a GIS survey. This is still configuration, not a new module.

LICS-3063.title: Confirm the land before buying a landowner permit
LICS-3063.why: Missouri landowner permits should not sell until the hunter confirms the land. A wrong tract is a compliance miss. Confirm at buy time.

LICS-3712.title: Turn land profiles on separately for businesses vs people
LICS-3712.why: Land profiles for a business and for a person should be turned on separately. Some agencies are ready for people and not for outfitters, or the reverse. PayIt-owned switch so we do not force both.

LICS-3886.title: Draw group: leader buys the quota, members buy a companion license
LICS-3886.why: A draw group needs the leader to buy the quota and members to buy a companion license, not six people fighting for the same tag. PayIt-owned pattern several states will use. Hunters already hunt this way in camp.

RESRV-431.title: Save or withdraw a volunteer signup for a specific event
RESRV-431.why: A volunteer should save or withdraw a signup for one event without calling the coordinator. Missouri and other event clients lose volunteers in a form they cannot undo. This is courtesy and data quality.

RESRV-435.title: Save, withdraw, or submit a volunteer application (not tied to one event)
RESRV-435.why: Volunteer applications (not tied to one event) also need save, withdraw, and submit. People start an application on the couch and finish later. Missouri and shared VEMS.

RESRV-772.title: Find events by proximity, calendar date, and category
RESRV-772.why: Hunters cannot find a class near them, on a date they can attend, in a category they care about. Proximity, calendar, and category are how people actually look. Minnesota, Missouri, Ohio, and anyone using events.

RESRV-773.title: Find volunteer shifts at events with location, date, and role filters
RESRV-773.why: Volunteer shift finding is the same problem: location, date, and role. Coordinators get no-shows when people cannot see what is open. Missouri and shared VEMS.

RESRV-775.title: Find volunteer roles with search, filters, and categories
RESRV-775.why: Volunteer roles are buried unless you already know the name. Search, filters, and categories let a new volunteer find 'range safety' without a staff email. Same states as event find.

SYST-1043.title: Hide contact info for judges, officers, and attorneys from public reports
SYST-1043.why: Ohio public reports still expose contact info for judges, officers, and attorneys. That is a safety and policy miss. Hide it on public output; staff tools can keep it.

SYST-2531.title: Customers can find a lost certification themselves
SYST-2531.why: Customers lose a certification and call the agency because they cannot look it up. Minnesota and others want the customer to find it themselves. Fewer tickets, same record.

SYST-2676.title: Collect SSN/DL only when required; treat foreign DL as an exemption
SYST-2676.why: SSN and driver license are collected when the sale does not need them, and a foreign DL is treated as missing. Collect only when required and treat a foreign DL as an exemption. Minnesota, Missouri, Ohio, and privacy audits all care.

SYST-2983.title: Watch-list report of sales, harvest, events, and lotteries for flagged customers
SYST-2983.why: Ohio needs a watch-list of sales, harvest, events, and lotteries for flagged customers. Investigators should not query four modules. One report is the job they bought.

SYST-3087.title: Group mailed credentials from the same sale consistently
SYST-3087.why: Credentials from the same sale mail as separate packets and confuse the household. Group them. Platform-wide fulfillment quality.

SYST-3217.title: Check new accounts against interstate revocation data before they can buy
SYST-3217.why: A revoked hunter from another state can still open an account and buy. Missouri and Ohio want interstate revocation checked before the first sale. This is compact enforcement, not a marketing flag.

SYST-3630.title: Search and reuse certification records instead of retyping
SYST-3630.why: Staff retype certification records that already exist, and then duplicates fight each other. Search and reuse. Missouri, Oregon, and shared hunter-ed.

SYST-3822.title: Email links land on the right web page after login
SYST-3822.why: Missouri email links dump people on the wrong web page after login, so they think the notice was a dead end. Land on the page the email promised. This is trust in every notice you send.

CALM-1563.title: Warn in the app when a link opens an outside site (hunter ed, partners)
CALM-1563.why: Ohio's app opens hunter-ed and partner sites with no warning, and people think they are still in the agency app. Warn when a link leaves. That is how you avoid phishing panic and lost sessions.

CALM-3413.title: Clearer mobile home screen and navigation (part 3)
CALM-3413.why: Third slice of the clearer mobile home and navigation. Same goal: hunters complete the job they opened the app for. Still not a visual restyle for its own sake.

CVEH-1648.title: Merge duplicate vehicle records
CVEH-1648.why: Mississippi has duplicate vehicle records for the same hull or VIN, so history and fees split. Merge them. Title staff cannot certify a file that exists twice.

CVEH-1757.title: Register a boat and its motor in one flow
CVEH-1757.why: A boat and its motor are one purchase in the real world and two registrations in CORE. Register them in one flow. Every boat client pays the extra counter time until this exists.

CVEH-1786.title: Save filters on vehicle application queues
CVEH-1786.why: Vehicle application queues reset filters every time, so staff re-click the same county and status. Save the filters. Louisiana, Minnesota, Mississippi back-office time.

CVEH-1799.title: Set vehicle renewal rules in Control Center
CVEH-1799.why: Renewal rules are still code instead of Control Center, so a season change is a project. Let the agency set vehicle renewal rules. Platform vehicle clients stop waiting on a release for a date.

FNCL-2043.title: Missouri-requested financials (part 1 of 2)
FNCL-2043.why: This is the first half of Missouri's contracted financials request pack—not one feature. It exists so COMO accounting, statements, and money tickets can close in this quarter. Brief the linked tickets, not this bucket name.

FNCL-74.title: Take cash and card (or multiple tenders) on a single sale
FNCL-74.why: A hunter pays cash and card on one sale and CORE cannot take both. Louisiana, Minnesota, Mississippi, and Ohio all see split tenders at the counter. Multiple tenders on one receipt is how people actually pay.

LICS-3304.title: Missouri-requested licensing (part 1 of 4)
LICS-3304.why: First slice of Missouri's contracted licensing requests, not a single product. Capacity is reserved so COMO licensing tickets can close. Use the linked tickets when you brief a customer.

LICS-3305.title: Missouri-requested licensing (part 2 of 4)
LICS-3305.why: Second slice of the same Missouri licensing request pack. Same rule: do not brief the bucket; brief the COMO tickets inside it.

LICS-3770.title: Missouri-requested licensing (part 3 of 4)
LICS-3770.why: Third slice of Missouri's licensing request pack. Still a delivery bucket for contracted tickets, not a new license type.

RESRV-1571.title: Range Class A/B check-in and check-out, orientation, and checkout survey
RESRV-1571.why: Ohio Class A and B ranges need check-in, check-out, orientation, and a checkout survey in CORE. Today that lives on clipboards. This is how an unmanned or lightly staffed range actually runs.

RESRV-437.title: Warn on duplicate locations and double-booked facilities; relax rigid seat limits
RESRV-437.why: Two classes get the same room, or seat limits are so rigid a reasonable overage dies. Warn on duplicate locations and double-books, and stop treating every seat count as sacred. Arkansas, Minnesota, Ohio, Oregon.

RESRV-447.title: Favorite people list and join events as a group
RESRV-447.why: People hunt and take classes as a group, then register one by one. Favorites and join-as-group is how families and clubs actually sign up. Minnesota and Missouri.

RESRV-485.title: Save a registration in progress, withdraw it, and clearer requirement steps
RESRV-485.why: A registration in progress cannot be saved or withdrawn, so people abandon or create duplicates. Clearer requirement steps tell them why they are stuck. Missouri, Ohio, and shared VEMS.

RESRV-774.title: Let guests search events and roles; create an account only when they register
RESRV-774.why: Guests should search events and volunteer roles before they create an account. Forcing a login first is why people leave. Account at register-time, not at browse-time.

SYST-4102.title: Missouri-requested platform (part 1 of 2)
SYST-4102.why: First half of Missouri's contracted platform request pack (Control Center, customer, cross-cutting tickets). Brief the COMO list, not the bucket. XXL because it is many tickets, not one screen.

CVEH-1158.title: Fuller vehicle history for research
CVEH-1158.why: Louisiana, Minnesota, and Mississippi research a hull and get a thin history. Fuller vehicle history is how they catch skipped transfers. This is investigative, not a new registration type.

CVEH-1301.title: Hide registration or title numbers until approved
CVEH-1301.why: Registration or title numbers show before the application is approved, and customers treat a draft as a credential. Hide numbers until approved. Platform-wide vehicle integrity.

CVEH-1423.title: Separate transfer vs add/remove owner (no transfer to yourself)
CVEH-1423.why: Transferring a vehicle and adding/removing an owner are different legal acts; CORE lets you 'transfer to yourself.' Split them. Every title shop knows the difference; the system should too.

CVEH-686.title: Structured registration and title questions by vehicle type
CVEH-686.why: Registration and title questions are a blob instead of a structure by vehicle type. A boat asks car questions and clerks skip or guess. PayIt-owned so later states inherit a sane form.

FNCL-2044.title: Missouri-requested financials (part 2 of 2)
FNCL-2044.why: Second half of Missouri's financials request pack. Same contracted tickets, later capacity. Brief COMO, not the epic title.

LICS-3771.title: Missouri-requested licensing (part 4 of 4)
LICS-3771.why: Fourth and last slice of Missouri's licensing request pack. Closes the contracted licensing list for that year. Still a bucket—use the linked tickets in a client meeting.

RESRV-1292.title: Missouri-requested events (part 1 of 2)
RESRV-1292.why: First half of Missouri's contracted events request pack. Education and volunteer tickets live here as a set. Brief the COMO events list, not 'MO requests.'

RESRV-1293.title: Missouri-requested events (part 2 of 2)
RESRV-1293.why: Second half of the Missouri events request pack. Same guidance: the value is in the linked tickets.

RESRV-490.title: Auto-mark volunteers inactive after they stop serving; staff can reinstate
RESRV-490.why: Volunteers stay 'active' forever, so coordinators cannot tell who still serves. Auto-inactivate after they stop, and let staff reinstate. Minnesota, Missouri, Ohio.

SYST-4103.title: Missouri-requested platform (part 2 of 2)
SYST-4103.why: Second half of Missouri's platform request pack. XXL for the same reason as part 1: many contracted tickets, one delivery bucket.

SYST-856.title: Merge duplicate customers into one surviving record
SYST-856.why: Duplicate customers split sales, harvest, and money across two people. Merge into one surviving record for Arkansas, Louisiana, Minnesota, and Missouri. This is how you stop refunding the wrong file.

LICS-3103.title: Save the calling number on a phone harvest check
LICS-3103.why: Ohio phone harvest checks do not keep the calling number, so a later dispute has no trail. Save it. Law enforcement and customer service both use that callback.

LICS-3773.title: Apply the 30-day repurchase window to permits that are not exclude-policy
LICS-3773.why: Ohio's 30-day repurchase window is skipped on permits that are not 'exclude-policy,' so a hunter buys again too soon or is blocked too long. Apply the window to the permits the rule actually names. Fairness at the counter.

LICS-3774.title: Harvest report with Ohio filters (game, county, ESA, flags) exportable to Excel
LICS-3774.why: Ohio harvest reporting needs their filters—game, county, ESA, flags—and an Excel export biologists already use. A generic dump does not file. This is how they manage the season, not a vanity report.

RESRV-456.title: Cancel or postpone a published event; keep students if postponed
RESRV-456.why: Ohio publishes an event and then weather or an instructor dies. They need to cancel or postpone without losing the students on a postpone. Today they delete and rebuild.

RESRV-460.title: Create a weekly or monthly event series instead of each date by hand
RESRV-460.why: Weekly and monthly classes are typed date by date. A series is how education actually schedules. Ohio staff time, fewer missed weeks.

RESRV-461.title: Unique-participant and historical attendance — not just today’s open events
RESRV-461.why: Event reports show who is on today's roster, not unique people over the year. Ohio cannot answer 'how many residents did we teach.' History and unique participants are the metric they owe leadership.

RESRV-462.title: Filter event reports by type, location, capacity, and volunteer roles
RESRV-462.why: Ohio event reports cannot filter by type, location, capacity, or volunteer roles, so they export and slice in Excel. Filters in CORE are how a coordinator runs the week.

RESRV-463.title: Allow a customer to hold seats at two events on the same day
RESRV-463.why: A customer cannot hold seats at two Ohio events on the same day, even when that is allowed. Families book a morning class and an evening hunt. Lift the false restriction.

SYST-1044.title: Track opens on emails and app messages sent from CORE
SYST-1044.why: Missouri and Ohio send email and app messages and cannot tell if anyone opened them. Open tracking is how you know a recall or a deadline notice landed. Not marketing spam—operational notices.

SYST-645.title: Control Center and counter usability fixes from client feedback
SYST-645.why: Control Center and counter usability fixes that clients already logged (Arkansas, Cherokee, Louisiana, Minnesota, Mississippi, Missouri). This is a pack of 'this screen fights me' items. Brief the tickets; the epic is the capacity.

LICS-2763.title: Collect and verify lottery partners before the permit is issued
LICS-2763.why: Ohio lottery partners are named after the permit is already issued, which is too late to verify. Collect and verify partners before issue. The regulation assumes the names are real.

LICS-2767.title: Stop a lottery application if the hunter does not meet the rules
LICS-2767.why: A hunter who does not meet lottery rules can still apply, then everyone sorts it out after the draw. Stop the application. Ohio staff time and fewer withdrawn winners.

LICS-3772.title: Run all lotteries of one type in one action (Ohio’s ~140-in-a-day case)
LICS-3772.why: Ohio runs on the order of 140 lotteries of one type in a day and should not click each one. One action for that type is the operational reality of their calendar. This is scale, not a new lottery product.

LICS-626.title: Citation and arrest reports in CORE (confirm scope with Ohio first)
LICS-626.why: Ohio wants citation and arrest reports in CORE. Confirm scope with them before we build a records system they did not mean. The why is officer reporting; the risk is boiling the ocean.

RESRV-1602.title: Staff can see youth-privacy flags and confirm contact email
RESRV-1602.why: Oregon staff must see youth-privacy flags and confirm the contact email before they message a family. Getting that wrong is a policy incident. Shared flag plus Oregon confirmation.

RESRV-1603.title: Print an event or class roster
RESRV-1603.why: Oregon instructors need a printed roster at the gate, not a phone in the sun. Print the event or class roster. Basic operations.

RESRV-1604.title: Clearer event error pages and FAQs
RESRV-1604.why: Oregon event errors dump people on a dead page with no FAQ. Clearer errors and FAQs are how a parent finishes registration without a call. Small and high-visibility.

RESRV-1605.title: Oregon event and volunteer reports in Control Center
RESRV-1605.why: Oregon event and volunteer reports belong in Control Center, not a side extract. Coordinators already live there. If it is not in CC, they will not use CORE as the system of record.

RESRV-420.title: Volunteer expenses and reimbursements, including personal vehicles
RESRV-420.why: Oregon volunteers drive personal vehicles and need expenses reimbursed. CORE has no place for that, so it lives in spreadsheets. Reimbursement is how they keep volunteers.

LICS-2663.title: Sell by one map (hunt area) and report harvest on another (deer permit area)
LICS-2663.why: Agencies sell by hunt area and report harvest on a different deer-permit map. Minnesota, Mississippi, and Ohio all have that split. One map for both is how harvest gets filed in the wrong place.

LICS-2766.title: After the hunt, the permit holder confirms which named partners showed up
LICS-2766.why: After the Ohio hunt, the permit holder must confirm which named partners actually showed up. Today that is a phone call or nothing. The regulation cares who was in the field.

LICS-2784.title: Add or change hunting partners on an awarded lottery permit
LICS-2784.why: Ohio lottery winners need to add or change hunting partners after the award, within the rules. A locked list means an illegal swap or a leftover name. This is post-draw life, not a new draw.

LICS-3790.title: Tie flags to the survey, limit officers to their county, use Ohio statuses
LICS-3790.why: Ohio enforcement flags should follow the survey, officers should only see their county, and statuses should be Ohio's. A national blob of flags is how the wrong officer acts on the wrong person.

LICS-624.title: ESA harvest messages and CWD test results to the hunter
LICS-624.why: Ohio hunters need ESA harvest messages and CWD test results in the channel they already use. If results live in a side mailbox, compliance and trust both drop. This is the close of the harvest loop.

CALM-3554.title: LED iOS builds and Apple Business Manager distribution to client devices
CALM-3554.why: Law-enforcement iOS builds still have to reach agency devices through Apple Business Manager. If that pipeline is not owned, officers stay on a stale build and a client cannot roll a fix. This is distribution, not a new LED feature.

SYST-3212.title: Missouri commercial print templates
SYST-3212.why: Missouri commercial print still uses the wrong templates, so a business license or receipt can print with the wrong layout. Staff reprint and customers walk with a document that does not match the sale. This is Missouri print, not a new product line.
